author: Jefferson Pan
title: Preston County passes EMS fee ordinance - NewsBreak
text:
By Jefferson Pan ,
5 hours ago
KINGWOOD, W.Va. (WBOY) — After loads of work and nearly 20 official drafts, the Preston County Commission voted unanimously to pass the EMS fee ordinance on Tuesday.
The commission has been working on the ordinance for years, getting up to draft 19, and has repeatedly said it’s needed to ensure ambulance coverage throughout the county.
Preston County EMS Director Henry McDonald said that the fee is needed to be able to pay for equipment, supplies and competitive wages for employees. The fiscal year for the fee will start July 1, with bills coming in the mail. Those bills will charge $90 per living unit per fiscal year, $60 for homestead residents (ones who are home-bound due to age or disability), $60 for recreational units, and $90 for business units in Preston County.
The fee also has a number of exemptions, including for those who have additional property for recreational use.
Factions in fight over MARL project prepare for public hearings next week “We hate to have to lay this at the feet of the residents to pay this. It’s not something we want to do, but we are thankful that this is now going to give us a reliable EMS system to serve the residents and visitors of the county,” McDonald told 12 News.
McDonald added that the county will continue to work with the state and federal government to find additional sources of funding for Preston County EMS with the aim of eventually being able to walk back the fee.
According to McDonald, the county is working on a draft of a contract with the four independent EMS agencies in the county that will allow them to access the ordinance money in exchange for greater financial oversight from the county.
